findings.title: Backup creation is not actually atomic — a crash leaves a partial/empty backup that looks valid
findings.description: The comment claims the backup is atomic, but `_unique_destination` creates the real destination directory (empty) up front via `mkdir`, then `create_backup` copies into a sibling temp dir and *moves the contents item-by-item into the already-existing destination*. During the entire copy/move window the destination exists and is non-empty-but-incomplete. If the process is killed (or the disk fills) mid-copy or mid-move, the destination remains as a partial or empty directory. `list_backups`/`get_backup` will treat it as a perfectly valid backup. A subsequent `restore_backup` from that partial backup overwrites the live save with incomplete/empty content → silent data loss. The only true-atomic approach is to copytree into the temp sibling and then `rename(temp -> destination)` as the final step, so the destination only ever appears once it is complete.
findings.suggestion: Reserve the name with a marker but copy into a temp sibling, then atomically `temp.rename(destination)` as the last operation. Do not pre-create `destination` and move contents into it. Alternatively, write a completion sentinel and have list/get/restore ignore directories lacking it.

findings.title: list_backups surfaces in-progress and orphaned temp/empty directories as real backups
findings.description: `create_backup` makes a temp dir named `.tmp-<timestamp>-XXXX` inside the save's backup folder (`destination.parent`), and also pre-creates the empty destination dir. `list_backups` iterates `save_dir.iterdir()` and accepts every directory (`if backup_dir.is_dir()`), with no filter for dotfiles or temp dirs. Consequently: (1) a concurrent backup (e.g. the watcher firing while the GUI renders) exposes the `.tmp-...` dir and the still-empty destination as backups; (2) if a backup crashes, the orphaned `.tmp-...` dir persists forever and is permanently listed as a (broken) backup. Restoring either yields garbage/empty saves.
findings.suggestion: Skip names starting with '.' (and specifically the `.tmp-` prefix) in `list_backups`. Better: clean up orphaned `.tmp-*` dirs on startup, and only list directories that contain real content / a completion marker.

findings.title: Configured debounce/cooldown are inconsistently applied (or ignored) when watching saves
findings.description: `api_watcher_toggle` computes `cooldown = config_get_all().get('backup_cooldown_minutes', 5) * 60` and passes it to `manager.watch(...)`, but never passes `debounce_seconds`, so the configured `debounce_seconds` is silently ignored and the hardcoded 5.0 default is always used. Worse, `api_watcher_save` (the per-save 'Watch' button) calls `manager.watch(save)` with NO arguments, so a save watched individually uses the hardcoded 300s cooldown and 5s debounce, ignoring the user's configured `backup_cooldown_minutes` entirely. Two code paths that should behave identically don't. There is also a default mismatch: `config.DEFAULTS['backup_cooldown_minutes']` is 1, `SaveWatcher`/`WatcherManager.watch` default to 300s, and the `.get(..., 5)` fallback here is yet another value.
findings.suggestion: Centralize watcher configuration: have `manager.watch` read debounce/cooldown from config (converting minutes→seconds) in one place, and call it the same way from both endpoints. Remove the conflicting hardcoded defaults.

findings.title: index() does O(all-backups) SQLite reads but only renders 50
findings.description: `index()` does `all_backups = list_backups()` (every backup across every save) and then `for b in all_backups:` builds `all_b`, opening `players.db` via `player_info(b.path)` and reading the note for EVERY backup. The template only renders `all_backups[:50]`. With hundreds/thousands of backups this opens hundreds of SQLite connections per page load while discarding all but 50 rows. Hot path.
findings.suggestion: Slice before the loop (`for b in all_backups[:50]:`) so player_info/note/thumbnail work is bounded by what's actually displayed.

findings.title: _save_info computes list_backups + slices [:5] per save but the result is never rendered
findings.description: `_save_info` calls `list_backups(save.game_mode, save.name)` for every save and builds a 5-element `backups` list into the returned dict. The saves card template never references `save.backups`. This is wasted I/O (a directory walk per save) on the page-render hot path, on top of the global `list_backups()` already done in `index()`. Combined with the unconditional `extract_all(path)` per save, page render cost scales with save count for data nobody sees.
findings.suggestion: Remove the per-save `list_backups`/`backups` computation from `_save_info`, or only compute it if the template actually displays it.

findings.title: CLI `config` value conversion raises uncaught ValueError, dumping a traceback
findings.description: In `config_command`, `value = float(value)` / `int(value)` are called with no try/except. `pz-saves config debounce_seconds abc` (or any non-numeric value for a numeric key) raises ValueError that propagates out of the Click command as an unhandled exception with a full Python traceback, instead of a friendly `ClickException`. Same for `int(value)` on the other numeric keys.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the conversions in try/except (ValueError, TypeError) and `raise click.ClickException(f"Invalid value for {key!r}: {value!r}")`. The GUI's `api_config` already does this correctly — mirror it.

findings.title: _do_backup holds the lock across the entire copytree, blocking the observer thread and pause()
findings.description: `_do_backup` performs `create_backup(...)` (a full directory copy of potentially thousands of map chunks — seconds to minutes on Windows w/ AV) while holding `self._lock`. `on_modified`, `pause`, `cancel_pending`, and `resume` all acquire the same lock, so during a backup the watchdog observer thread blocks on `on_modified`, and a concurrent restore's `pause_for(...)` → `pause()` blocks until the copy finishes. This can stall event delivery and defeats the purpose of `pause()` (a restore could be forced to wait for an in-flight backup, then the grace window may already be wrong).
findings.suggestion: Read/update the bookkeeping fields (`_last_backup_time`, `_last_backup_mtime`, cooldown/mtime checks) under the lock, then release the lock and run `create_backup` outside it. Re-check/guard re-entrancy with a separate 'backup in progress' flag if needed.

findings.title: rename_backups_for_save collision handling is platform-dependent and contradicts its docstring
findings.description: The docstring states it 'Raises BackupError if the new name already has backups (to avoid silently merging two histories)', but the function performs no explicit collision check — it relies on `old_dir.rename(new_dir)` failing. On POSIX, `rename` onto an existing *empty* directory succeeds silently (and onto a non-empty one raises ENOTEMPTY); on Windows it raises if the target exists at all. So an empty `new_dir` would be replaced rather than rejected, contradicting the contract. The GUI/CLI rely on `preflight_rename` for the real check, but this function is public and documents a guarantee it doesn't enforce.
findings.suggestion: Explicitly check `if new_dir.exists(): raise BackupError(...)` at the top, or fix the docstring to state that callers must run `preflight_rename` first.

findings.title: Dead initial assignments in parse_world_dictionary
findings.description: `total = 0`, `vanilla = 0`, `modded = 0` are assigned and then unconditionally overwritten (`total = len(ids)`, `vanilla = len(...)`, `modded = len(...)`). The initial assignments are dead code.
findings.suggestion: Remove the redundant initial assignments.

findings.title: _should_skip returns a re.Match/None, not bool, despite -> bool annotation
findings.description: `_should_skip` is annotated `-> bool` but returns `match() or search() or search()`, i.e. a `re.Match` object or `None`. It works under `if not _should_skip(...)`, but the return type is misleading and could surprise callers expecting a real bool.
findings.suggestion: Wrap in `bool(...)`.

findings.title: on_backup typed with builtin `callable` instead of typing.Callable
findings.description: `on_backup: callable | None = None` uses the builtin function `callable` as a type annotation. It's harmless under `from __future__ import annotations` (annotations not evaluated), but it's semantically wrong and tools won't treat it as a callable type.
findings.suggestion: Use `Callable[[BackupRecord], None] | None` from `typing`.

findings.title: Unused `import flask` in gui_command --no-browser branch
findings.description: `gui_command` does `import flask` in the `--no-browser` branch but never uses the `flask` module (it imports `app` from `.gui` separately). Dead import.
findings.suggestion: Remove `import flask`.

findings.title: player_info coerces falsy coordinates to 0 via truthiness, conflating valid 0/None
findings.description: `"x": round(row[2]) if row[2] else 0` (and y, z) uses truthiness to guard against None, but this also maps a legitimate coordinate of exactly 0.0 (or a very small float that rounds to 0) to 0. While 0.0→0 is harmless numerically, the pattern is fragile and hides the difference between 'unknown/None' and 'origin'. If a column is genuinely NULL you silently report 0 rather than indicating missing data.
findings.suggestion: Use an explicit None check: `round(row[2]) if row[2] is not None else None` (or 0 if a numeric default is desired), so NULL vs 0 is distinguishable.

findings.title: test_save_watcher_debounce asserts nothing about backup behavior
findings.description: The test fires one event and only asserts `watcher._last_event > 0`. The comment admits 'backup may fail in test'. It does not verify the debounce timer actually fires the backup, nor that cooldown/mtime guards behave. It essentially tests that an attribute was set, giving false confidence about the debounce logic.
findings.suggestion: Monkeypatch `create_backup` (as the other watcher tests do) and assert it is invoked exactly once after the debounce interval, and not invoked before.

findings.title: config.set_ read-modify-write is not synchronized — concurrent writes lose updates
findings.description: `set_` does `data = _load(); data[key] = value; _save(data)`. The file write itself is atomic (temp + os.replace), but the read-modify-write is not. The GUI server is multi-threaded and the watcher runs on its own thread; two near-simultaneous `set_`/`api_config` calls (or a config write during a watcher-triggered config read) can interleave so the last writer overwrites the other's change (lost update).
findings.suggestion: Guard `_load`/`_save` in `set_` with a module-level threading.Lock (and ideally a file lock for cross-process safety).

findings.title: get_backups reads _backups without the lock
findings.description: `get_backups` does `list(self._watchers[key]._backups)` with no lock held, while `_do_backup` appends to the same list under `self._lock`. Iterating/copying a list while another thread mutates it can raise or yield an inconsistent snapshot. It also reaches into a protected attribute.
findings.suggestion: Acquire the watcher's lock when copying `_backups`, or expose a thread-safe accessor on SaveWatcher.

findings.title: map_name fallback can return arbitrary binary-derived garbage
findings.description: When UTF-16LE decoding doesn't yield a plausible name, the fallback builds a string from every byte in range 32..126 across the whole file remainder and returns the first 80 chars. For a binary file this produces meaningless ASCII soup that gets surfaced as a 'map name'. The thresholds (len>2, len<100, [:80]) are unexplained magic numbers.
findings.suggestion: Tighten the fallback (e.g. require a contiguous printable run, validate against expected characters) or return None when confidence is low. Name the magic numbers as constants.

findings.title: watch() after stop() schedules on a dead Observer
findings.description: `WatcherManager.watch` always calls `self._observer.schedule(...)` immediately. After `stop()`, `self._observer` is a stopped (dead) Observer that cannot be restarted; `start()` only recreates the Observer when it is not alive. If a save is watched while the manager is stopped (e.g. `api_watcher_save` when `manager.running` is False), `watch` schedules on the dead observer before `start()` recreates a fresh one, potentially raising or leaking an emitter on the discarded observer. The subsequent `start()` reschedules from `_watchers`, so it usually self-corrects, but the initial schedule on the dead observer is fragile.
findings.suggestion: Only call `self._observer.schedule` when the observer is alive; otherwise just register in `_watchers` and let `start()` schedule everything when it (re)creates the Observer.

findings.title: Underscore loop variable `_` is actually used in size_mb/file_count
findings.description: `BackupRecord.file_count` and `size_mb` use `for _ in self.path.rglob('*') if _.is_file()` — `_` is conventionally a throwaway, but here it's dereferenced (`_.is_file()`, `_.stat()`). This is misleading to readers who scan for `_` as 'unused'.
findings.suggestion: Rename `_` to `p`/`f` for clarity.

findings.title: api_shutdown relies on removed werkzeug.server.shutdown and falls back to os._exit
findings.description: `request.environ.get('werkzeug.server.shutdown')` was removed in Werkzeug 2.1+, so on modern installs this is always None and the path falls through to `sys.exit(0)` (kills only the timer thread) and finally `os._exit(0)`, a hard exit that bypasses atexit/finally handlers and could interrupt an in-flight backup/restore on another thread (the watcher is stopped first, but a GUI-triggered restore is not). The 3s Timer is a best-effort guess for response flush.
findings.suggestion: Document that os._exit is the real shutdown mechanism, ensure no long-running write operation can be in flight at shutdown (or join them), and consider a cleaner signal-based stop.

overall_assessment: The codebase is generally careful about the security invariants it set out to protect (path traversal, symlink skipping, restore rollback, logged watcher errors) and has decent test coverage for those. However, the headline 'atomic backup' invariant is not actually atomic: the destination directory is created and populated in place, so a crash leaves a partial/empty backup that the listing/restore code cannot distinguish from a good one — a real data-loss path. There are also concrete correctness bugs in configuration plumbing (debounce/cooldown ignored or applied inconsistently between the two watch entry points), a couple of clear performance regressions on the GUI hot path (O(all-backups) SQLite reads, per-save unused list_backups), and an unguarded CLI conversion that crashes with a traceback. Most other items are minor robustness/convention issues.
summary: 1 blocker (non-atomic backup → data loss), several major bugs (temp dirs listed as backups, ignored/inconsistent debounce & cooldown config, O(all) GUI backup reads, wasted per-save list_backups, lock held across copytree, uncaught CLI ValueError), plus assorted minor edge-case, concurrency, and convention findings.
